'''Sir'''<ref name=":0" /> '''John Bernard Pethica''' (born 1953) is a British chemist and [[Science Foundation Ireland]] (S.F.I.) professor of [[material science]] at [[Trinity College, Dublin]], Chief Scientific Advisor at the UK's [[National Physical Laboratory (United Kingdom)|National Physical Laboratory]], and a visiting professor at [[Oxford University]]. Pethica is most noted for his work on the development of [[nanoindentation]] and atom resolution [[atomic force microscopy]].<ref name=":1">{{Cite web |title=Professor Sir John Pethica |url=https://www.stx.ox.ac.uk/people/john-pethica-0 |access-date=2025-06-04 |website=www.stx.ox.ac.uk |language=en}}</ref>

==Education==
John Pethica was a pupil at [[St Ambrose College]] in [[Hale Barns]], [[Trafford]], [[Manchester]]. He studied natural sciences (physics) at [[Trinity Hall, Cambridge]], graduating with a B.A and a Ph.D. from the [[University of Cambridge]] during the late 1970s.<ref>{{Who's Who | title = PETHICA, Sir John Bernard | id = U41813 | volume = 2025 | edition = online}}</ref><ref name=":0">{{Cite web |last= |first= |title=Knighthood for Professor John Pethica |url=https://www.tcd.ie/news_events/articles/knighthood-for-professor-john-pethica/ |access-date=2025-05-27 |website=www.tcd.ie |publisher=Trinity College Dublin |language=en}}</ref>

==Career==
Pethica was a scientist employed at [[Brown, Boveri & Cie]] in Switzerland from 1980 to 1982.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Microscopy: Advances, Innovation, Impact 2016 |url=https://www.rms.org.uk/rms-event-calendar/microscopy-advances-innovation-impact-2016.html |access-date=2025-06-04 |website=www.rms.org.uk |language=en}}</ref> After this he held the position of Fellow at the University of Cambridge from 1983 to 1987. He became a lecturer at The [[University of Oxford]] in 1996, subsequently assuming the role of Professor of Materials Science.<ref name=":1" />

In 2001, Pethica was one of the first ten people awarded an S.F.I. principal investigator award. Following the award, he transferred his activities from [[Oxford]] to [[Dublin]], becoming an SFI Research Professor in Trinity College Dublin.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Dublin |first=Trinity College |title=TCD Professor Appointed Vice President and Physical Sciences Secretary of Royal Society |url=https://www.tcd.ie/news_events/articles/tcd-professor-appointed-vice-president-and-physical-sciences-secretary-of-royal-society/ |access-date=2025-06-04 |website=www.tcd.ie |language=en}}</ref>

In February 2005, it was announced that Pethica will be the director of the Naughton Institute which will house [[CRANN]], a new purpose built [[nanotechnology]] centre in Trinity College Dublin.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Professor Sir John Pethica |url=https://www.trinhall.cam.ac.uk/people/professor-sir-john-pethica/ |access-date=2025-06-04 |website=Trinity Hall Cambridge |language=en-GB}}</ref>

In October 2007, Pethica was made the Chief Scientific Advisor at the UK's [[National Physical Laboratory (United Kingdom)|National Physical Laboratory]], the UK's National Measurement Institute.<ref name=":2">{{Cite web |title=Fellow Detail Page {{!}} Royal Society |url=https://royalsociety.org/sitecore/content/royal-society/configuration/foundation/dynamics-api/fellowsdetailpage/ |access-date=2025-06-04 |website=royalsociety.org |language=en}}</ref>

==Honours and awards==
In 1999, Pethica was elected a [[Fellow of the Royal Society]] (FRS).<ref name=":3" /> He has also served as Vice-President and Physical Secretary of the Royal Society. He was elected a [[Fellow of the Royal Academy of Engineering]] (FREng) in 2013.<ref name=":3">{{cite web|title=List of Fellows|url=http://www.raeng.org.uk/about-us/people-council-committees/the-fellowship/list-of-fellows|access-date=23 October 2014|archive-date=8 June 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160608094405/http://www.raeng.org.uk/about-us/people-council-committees/the-fellowship/list-of-fellows|url-status=dead}}</ref> He was elected an [[honorary fellow]] of both Trinity College Dublin (in 2011) and [[St Cross College, Oxford]] (in 2014).<ref name=":0" /><ref>{{cite web|title=Sir John Pethica Elected to Honorary Fellowship|url=http://www.stx.ox.ac.uk/about-st-cross/news/sir-john-pethica-elected-honorary-fellowship|website=News|publisher=St Cross College, Oxford|accessdate=9 November 2014|archive-date=19 December 2014|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141219062132/http://www.stx.ox.ac.uk/about-st-cross/news/sir-john-pethica-elected-honorary-fellowship|url-status=dead}}</ref>

Pethica was awarded the Rosenhain Medal & Prize from the [[Institute of Materials, Minerals and Mining]] in 1997.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Rosenhain Medal & Prize (not available in 2025) |url=https://www.iom3.org/award/rosenhain-medal-prize-not-available-in-2025.html |access-date=2025-06-04 |website=www.iom3.org |publisher=IOM3}}</ref> He was the 2001 recipient of the [[Hughes Medal]] of the Royal Society of London,<ref name=":2" /> and the 2002 recipient of the [[Fernand Holweck Medal and Prize|Holweck Prize]] from the [[Institute of Physics]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Professor John Bernard Pethica|url=http://www.iop.org/about/awards/bilateral/holweck/medallists/page_60680.html|publisher=[[Institute of Physics]]|accessdate=14 June 2014}}</ref>

Pethica was [[Knight Bachelor|knighted]] in the [[2014 Birthday Honours]] for services to science.<ref>{{London Gazette |issue=60895 |date=14 June 2014 |page=b2 |supp=y}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|title=Oxford food bank founders made MBEs in Queen's Birthday Honours|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/uk-england-oxfordshire-27794561|work=BBC News|date=14 June 2014}}</ref>

==Personal life==
Pethica is a musician – playing violin and other instruments – with a particular interest in [[Irish folk music|Irish]] and [[British folk music]].
